revision: 2 - rewritten after an adversarial pass upheld three showstoppers against revision 1: unit substitution (BTE vs preload ceiling), per-call vs per-turn modelling, and the omitted S6 row.
cost_unit: BTE = billed-token-equivalent = input tokens x price multiplier (1.0 plain / 1.25 write / 0.1 read). A COST unit. NEVER compared to a preload-token budget.

assumptions.assumption: Cache WRITE = 1.25x base input rate, cache READ = 0.1x, default 5-minute ephemeral TTL.
assumptions.status: TAKEN FROM THE BRIEF, NOT RE-VERIFIED against current pricing.
assumptions.falsified_by: pricing docs showing different multipliers, or adoption of the 1h TTL (2.0x write).
assumptions.sensitivity: linear - every BTE figure scales directly with these two numbers.

assumptions.assumption: Token counts are the tiktoken/cl100k_base proxy from econ_segments.py.
assumptions.status: DECLARED PROXY - Claude's tokenizer is not public and the API is credit-blocked.
assumptions.sensitivity: RATIOS between programmes are far more robust than absolute magnitudes.

assumptions.assumption: A cache hit needs byte-identity AND the request inside the TTL.
assumptions.status: NOW PARTLY MEASURED (op-burst proxy, econ_gaps.py), not asserted.
assumptions.falsified_by: instrumented CHAT-turn timings, which would beat this op-burst proxy.
assumptions.sensitivity: decides how much weight the COLD column deserves.

assumptions.assumption: Billed input tokens are computed on Anthropic's canonical rendering of the tool definitions, not the client's JSON bytes.
assumptions.status: STRUCTURAL LIMIT ON ANY LOCAL ESTIMATE.
assumptions.falsified_by: a funded count_tokens call on the same tools array.
assumptions.sensitivity: the panel's two serializations differ 24% on an identical tool set.

assumptions.assumption: The reconstructed sessions are representative in SHAPE, not recordings.
assumptions.status: RECONSTRUCTED FROM SHIPPED CODE. The brief's oracle asked for 3 REAL turns; none exist. This is a NAMED ORACLE MISS, not a satisfied requirement.
assumptions.falsified_by: a captured transcript of real panel turns.

assumptions.assumption: A changed SYSTEM block still leaves the TOOLS breakpoint hittable, because prefix order is tools -> system -> messages and matching is longest-prefix.
assumptions.status: NOT OBSERVED LIVE. Follows from documented ordering; no live request was made.
assumptions.falsified_by: a live request showing cache_read_input_tokens = 0 when only the system block changed.
assumptions.sensitivity: LOAD-BEARING. If false, tools become a 1.25x write on every first call and every cached row gets materially worse.

assumptions.assumption: Within one user turn, tool-loop iterations 2..k hit the cache: seconds apart, byte-identical tools array, frozen system string.
assumptions.status: CODE-VERIFIED for byte-identity (claude_worker.py:85 stores the system string once; :157 passes the same self._tools every iteration). The cache behaviour itself is NOT observed live.
assumptions.falsified_by: the same live request A6 needs.
assumptions.sensitivity: LOAD-BEARING and it INVERTS revision 1's conclusion. At k=1 caching can be a net penalty; at k>=2 it wins decisively.

grounding_source.column_used: tokens_model_visible - what the model is charged after the double JSON encode (C1-F8). Revision 1 used the smaller 'tokens' column without stating the choice.

verdict.the_question: Is T.1 the right first mile, or is a cache-control change?
verdict.the_answer: They are NOT alternatives - they optimise DIFFERENT QUANTITIES. T.1 reduces context-window occupancy (preload tokens); caching reduces price (BTE). The brief poses them as 'opposite engineering programmes' and that framing is the error: a cache read cannot put anything under a preload-token ceiling, and a tool-surface reduction cannot make a cached token cheaper. Measured, BOTH are worth doing, and S6 - both plus the volatile fix - is the cheapest row in every regime measured.

preload_tokens._what_this_is: CONTEXT-WINDOW OCCUPANCY in tokens. This is what harness/verify/token_ceiling.json:max_preload_tokens budgets, and it is the quantity T.1 reduces.
preload_tokens._caching_does_not_change_it: A cache read changes what a token COSTS. The tokens still occupy the window, still consume attention, and still count against the ceiling. Revision 1 compared a cost figure to this budget; that was a unit substitution, corrected here.
preload_tokens.verdict: OVER the ceiling on every surface under every reading. Caching does NOTHING for this quantity. On preload tokens, T.1 is the ONLY lever.

cost_BTE._what_this_is: PRICE in billed-token-equivalents (BTE) = input tokens x multiplier. A cost unit, never comparable to a preload-token ceiling.
cost_BTE.verdict: Caching cuts the PRICE of the tool span by 90% per cache-read call. It does not cut its SIZE at all.

ttl_evidence.reading: Revision 1 asserted artist think-time 'routinely exceeds 5 minutes' with NO producer, and used it to argue the cache would usually be cold. Measured on this machine's audit log, at a 30s burst threshold 36.8% of inter-burst gaps exceed the TTL - so the majority fall INSIDE it. The assertion is not supported; COLD is a real regime but not the common one.
ttl_evidence.bias: An artist may think for a long time WITHOUT firing an operation, and a single chat turn fires several operations. Collapsing ops into bursts corrects the second and cannot correct the first, so this figure is best read as a LOWER BOUND on how often the cache is cold - the true cold fraction is at least this and possibly higher. It is a proxy, and it replaces an assertion that had no evidence at all.

small_scene.note: Per-API-CALL occupancy at turn 3 with k=2 calls/turn, grounding RESIDENT in history rather than a separate transient line. The four rows are DISJOINT: conversation_chat excludes grounding, so the shares are a real partition. Revision 1's rows overlapped and its shares were not a partition.

The four rows are DISJOINT: conversation_chat excludes grounding, so the shares are a real partition. Revision 1's rows overlapped and its shares were not a partition.

large_scene_spread.note: Revision 1 asserted 'every scenario lands within 3% of ~119k BTE'. Computed rather than asserted, the spread is far wider. The surviving claim is the RANKING (grounding dominates), not a narrow band.

tokenizer_and_serialization_band.why: Same tool set, two defensible local serializations, 24% apart. Anthropic re-renders tool definitions canonically (A4), so neither is the billed number.
